annotations.text:
A LEARNED FEED, NOT A SUBSCRIPTION.

No sections, no shelves, no interest axis: the next post is whatever the ranking picked. The interest survives as a TAG on the post — it is what the model learns over, not the shape of the screen.

The chrome gets out of the way so the post is the screen, and the signals (like, comment, save, share) sit where a thumb already rests.

THE SECOND SCREEN IS NOT OPTIONAL.

A feed learned from behaviour needs a way to see why and to say no — otherwise the only way to correct it is to stop using it. It also names the signals being collected in plain words, which is where Principle III lands once dwell time is being measured.

WHAT THIS COSTS, so the decision is deliberate:

· Constitution Principle I ("Interest Is the Organising Principle", NON-NEGOTIABLE) and 001/FR-033 are replaced. The negative test that guards them would be deleted, not adjusted.
· New machinery none of which exists: dwell-time telemetry from the client, a per-viewer signal store, and a ranking service between the datastore and the feed.
· D1 (read-time assembly) was forced by FR-017 + SC-009 — a visibility flip must land everywhere immediately. A ranked feed still has to pass VisibilityFilter at read time, so ranking chooses CANDIDATES and the filter still decides.
· Dwell tracking is behavioural data collection. That is why the tuning sheet names the signals rather than hiding them.
